desc:
Hills cover this landscape , and their size grow towards the west. Every rise,
valley, and hilltop is covered with dark, brooding trees, most of them fir or
birch. The hills here are dwarfed by a plateau, a higher part of Dol Guldur,
which towers to the north and northwest.
name: Dark and Sloping Forest

desc:
Forest covers these slopes, conspiring with the plateau to the north to keep
these woods in permanent shadows. The slopes ascend gently towards the west,
slowly climbing towards higher heights. The trees are gnarled and ancient, some
of them true behemoths that must have been standing here since the the time of
the last alliance.
name: Craggy Slope beneath a Plateau

desc:
The trees of this forest are towering, ancient giants. Many of them are gnarled
and twisted. Large roots protrude through the thick layer of rotting leaves on
the ground. Aside from the trees, little grows here except and the fungi and
mushrooms that draw their nourishment from the tree's trunks, as little light
finds its way through the canopy.
name: Dark and Dreary Corner of Mirkwood

desc:
These shrub-covered fields lie in the shadow of a high plateau to the west, and
that shade probably kept the trees of Mirkwood to the east from creeping all the
way up to the foot of the plateau. The vegetation consists of thorn-covered
bushes and sturdy-looking shrubs.
name: Tangled, Ensnaring Thornbushes

desc:
This thicket-covered stretch of land lies between denser undergrowth to the
north, the dark depths of Mirkwood to the east, and a plateau to the west. The
ground is overgrown with thorny thickets cut with wide paths. Most of the bushes
have long, nasty thorns pointing every which way.
name: Tangled Thornbushes

desc:
The uneven terrain here at the foot of the high plateau to the west is entirely
covered by immense thickets. Thousands of shrubs grow in such proximity that to
each other that the whole thicket appears like one single plant. A few paths
exist where a mount or traveller can make their way through.
name: Thorny Thicket

desc:
The slopes of this hill are covered by a dark forest. The trees are black oaks
with gnarled roots and twisted trunks, and tall, dark alders. The undergrowth of
strangling vines and long-thorned bushes has been haphazardly crushed and torn
up, root and all, as if something very large and impatient smashed through.
name: Dark Wooded Hill

desc:
Raised over the surrounding dark forest, this hill might once have been lit by
the warm sun. But now the black oaks have stolen most of the light with their
dense cover of dark leaves. The hill's summit and slopes are covered by a layer
of dead leaves and several large, round boulders.
name: Steep, Sombre Hill

desc:
This brush-covered area is squeezed between dark woods to the north and a steep
plateau to the south. The ground is very stony, but the poor soil seems adequate
for a variety of plantlife consisting of brown, tough shrubs, wild grass, as
well as some larger thornbushes.
name: Brush in the Shadow of a Plateau

desc:
This patch of brushland is squeezed between the forest to the north and a
plateau to the south. The plantlife consists mainly of low, brown shrubs and
long, thorny vines that creep across the ground for lack of trees to climb. The
plateau to the south overshadows these lower lands, casting them into gloom for
much of the day.
name: Brush between Mirkwood and a Plateau

desc:
Black oaks and alders make up this part of the forest. Their limbs and leaves
form a dense ceiling that blocks out all light. The ground is soft and muddy and
the air is stagnant. Sickly grey-green lichen and patches of fungi cover many of
the trunks.
name: Adumbral Mirkwood

desc:
Here, in the depth of Mirkwood, the land is shrouded in shadows and mirk by the
thick layers of branch and leaf overhead. The air is humid and stagnant with the
smells of rot and decay. Thick layers of fallen leaves, knee-deep in some
places, cover the forest floor.
name: Under Adumbral Canopies

desc:
Bleak and bare hills form this windswept plateau. The forest covering the lower
hills is here replaced by a few struggling brambles and weeds. The plateau
extends in all directions for miles and its edges are sharp and steep. The only
way down seems to be the slope to the west.
name: Bleak, Windswept Plateau

desc:
The bare and flat ground extends in all directions except towards the east where
a sudden drop marks the border of the plateau. There are no trees here, and
vegetation is sparse. The windswept heights hold little topsoil except what's
trapped in small cracks.
name: Edge of a Bleak Plateau

desc:
This plateau rises above the forest to the east and north. Its windswept heights
look down on the dark canopy. The flat surface of the plateau has very little
soil, mostly it is bare, black rock. At one place boulders are piled in a
half-circle, as if someone tried to build a windshelter here, but it looks like
it would provide little shelter.
name: Corner of a Windswept Plateau

desc:
A steep rise ascends from the lower plateau to this higher promontory. Bare,
black rock covers the ground and no plant or tree grow here. The promontory
overlooks the lower forest to the west and to the north, but the canopy is too
dense to see through. Far to the west a rocky outcrop stands out against the sky
with the main part of Dol Guldur beyond it.
name: Rocky Promontory

desc:
The flat plateau is crossed by a shallow ravine filled with brambles and
boulders. Little grows on top of the windswept plateau where the ground is black
rock with barely any soil. The few straggly trees that do grow here are sad
looking things with thin branches and few leaves.
name: At a Ravine on a Plateau

desc:
Some twisted, scraggly birches accompanied by dry, brown bushes are the only
signs of life on this otherwise desolate plateau. The lower land south and east
is covered by a dense forest, but is unreachable due to the steep sides of the
plateau.
name: Bleak, Windswept Plateau

desc:
This cave has been dug directly out of the plateau. The floor is rough stone,
but piles of eroded dirt blur the lines between the walls and the ground. A
hitching post and feed trough line one wall, surrounded by a ring of brown,
dried, droppings. Clearly the occupants are not overly concerned with cleaning.
To the other side, a few logs have been set around a crude fire pit.
name: Hollowed Cave

desc:
The slopes of these gentle hills are covered with birch and fir, while the
hilltops are dominated by gnarly old oaks. Their crowns are wide and dense,
casting the land into an everlasting darkness. Faint murmurs rustle through the
leaves as the wind stirs them, as if the trees whisper to one another in hushed
voices.
name: Shaded Mirkwood Hillock

desc:
Gentle, rolling hillocks cover the lands in this part of Mirkwood. Slopes,
hilltops and long valleys continue in every direction except toward the west
where a sudden drop puts a halt to any consideration of travel. The sturdy
trees, ancient-looking behemoths, are covered in ensnaring vines and moss in
various shades of green and grey.
name: Slopes of a Mirkwood Hillock

desc:
The round, softly sloped hills in this area are covered with a dense, strange
looking forest. Most of the trees are oaks that grew tall and strong, but their
bark is almost black. A few ashes and pines stand between the oaks. The
undergrowth is thick, with many thorny climbing vines that conceal some nasty
little cracks in the ground. A sharp edged cliff protects the hills to the west,
while to the east the land changes to a plain forest.
name: Forested Mirkwood Hillocks

desc:
These woods are dark and gloomy, no sky is visible through the ceiling of
leaves. The trees are mostly dark oaks with rough bark and thick branches laden
with leaves. Due to the lack of light, little brush grows under the trees. Dead
leaves cover the ground in a thick layer of rotting plant material, adding an
unpleasant aroma.
name: Sinister Forest

desc:
The forest is extremely dark and dense, with huge trees that prevent any
sunlight from reaching the ground. A crude camp was set up between some large
rocks and ancient trees. It consists of a few ragged furs and dirty hides around
a fireplace. A huge dulled, dirty cauldron, used to cook something or someone,
hangs over the fire.
name: Camp of the Hill Trolls

desc:
This tunnel has been hollowed out by the hill trolls out of the black rock that
makes up Dol Guldur. A rough stair leads back upwards into the forest that seems
to have been a natural cave at some point in time.
name: Tunnel of the Hill Trolls

desc:
The forest rises to cover a wide but low hill. The trees are old, black oaks in
the lower parts and tall firs higher up. They form a dense ceiling, beneath
which the shadows reign. Little grows here but the ground is covered in dead,
rotting leaves.
name: Deep Forested Hillock

desc:
The valley floor is covered with a dense and dark wood of ancient oaks, which
block most of what sunlight there might be above. The valley continues to the
south while gentle slopes rise to the north and west, leading up to higher
ground, which even so look equally covered by dense forest.
name: Deep Forested Valley

desc:
The floor of this wide valley is covered by enormous oaks. It narrows to the
north while the south side is blocked off by slopes too steep to ascend. Fallen
leaves cover the ground in a thick layer of rotting compost. The smell of rotten
plantlife hangs heavily in the air.
name: Deep Forested Valley

desc:
The branches of this tree form a loose canopy. The footing is treacherous, but
plentiful. Rotten vegetation clings to the trunk, giving off an unpleasant
odour. The tree itself seems solid, though it has hard to tell behind the
multiple layers of moss.
name: Up an Oak Tree

desc:
No light reaches the ground of this forest. The crowns of the trees block the
sunlight completely. The old oaks are black and have a strangeness about them.
Most of them did not grow straight, their trunks are twisted and their roots
seem to wrestle with each other to get the most nutrients from the soil.
name: Looming Trees

desc:
The ground under the dark canopy is soft and muddy. The trees are mostly oaks
and alders that look like they have stood here since an earlier age. The alders
surround a small sinkhole filled with murky, muddy water that smells of sulphur.
The deep tracks of large foot prints leading to the water show that it is
potable for at least some kind of creature.
name: At a Black Forest Pond

desc:
Tall dark trees dominate these rolling hills, their leaf-covered branches
forming an almost solid ceiling above. Little sun ever reaches the ground and as
a result the undergrowth is very sparse. The hills expand in all directions
except to the south, where there is a steep drop.
name: Densely Forested Hillock

desc:
This forested hillock is elevated over the lower parts of Mirkwood to the east
and north. The same gnarly ancients grow here though, their massive trunks
standing a tad too close to each other. Their outstretched branches intertwine
above to form an almost solid ceiling of vegetation.
name: Gloomy Hillock

desc:
The dark tunnel suddenly stops in what seems to be dead end. A few splintered
crates, some completely upended, have been dumped unceremoniously at the end of
the tunnel. Some roots grow down from the forest above amongst the troll filth.
name: Tunnel of the Hill Trolls

desc:
The walls of the tunnel are stricken with claw marks that can be seen leading to
the south and east where they finally disappear into darkness. A foetid smell of
rotting flesh reeks from the southern tunnel.
name: Tunnel of the Hill Trolls

desc:
The tunnel suddenly opens into a large cave that has been turned into a foul
larder. Rotting corpses hang from crude hooks to preserve the meat and prevent
any worms from reaching the flesh. The only way out of here is to head back
north through the tunnel where the air smells slightly cleaner.
name: Larder of the Hill Trolls
